newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - L&G to report steady progress.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - L&G to report steady progress.

text.p: Life assurer Legal and General Group Plc (L&G) will bring the curtain down on the results season among the UK's FTSE-100 listed insurance companies next week when it reports annual profits for 1996 on Thursday.
At the half-year stage operating profits rose to 134.3 million stg from 111.1 million stg, fueled by strong life and pensions sales in Britain.
In January, L&G new business figures for 1996 showed worldwide growth of 36 percent and 54 percent in the UK. New pensions business grew by 25 percent.
Regular premium income in the UK rose 23 percent to 153 million stg while one-off premiums jumped to 1.2 billion stg from 543 million stg in 1995.
"People will be looking to see what they say about new business. It would appear the market is quite buoyant at the moment," said one analyst.
Profit forecasts range between 271 and 348 million pounds compared with 271.3 million stg last year. The dividend is expected to be raised to 11.1 pence per share.
Last July the group sold its commercial general insurance business to Guardian Royal Exchange producing an exceptional pre-tax profit of about 72 million stg.
The disposal was part of L&G's strategy of concentrating on life insurance and other personal lines of business, including motor and household insurance.
In a recent note, Lehman analyst Rob Procter said that the strength of the figures marked a clear return to growth after the difficult years of 1994 and 1995.
In terms of profitability of new business, there was a strengthening in the first half and he said he expected this trend to have continued up to the year-end.

The company said it had increased market share by cutting prices on policies through all distribution channels. L&G chief executive David Prosser said it had been reducing gross margins to build back net margins with volume.
The company has been identified in the past as a potential takeover or merger candidate, though L&G has repeatedly dismissed such rumours.
It has also ruled out talk of acquisitions. At the half-year stage chief executive David Prosser stated that they did not form part of the group's strategy and that the focus was on organic growth.
